caseName: St. Paul, Minneapolis & Manitoba Railway Co. v. Minnesota ex rel. City of Minneapolis
caseNameFull: ST. PAUL, MINNEAPOLIS & MANITOBA RAILWAY COMPANY v. STATE OF MINNESOTA ex rel. CITY OF MINNEAPOLIS
syllabus: Affirmed on authority of Northern Pacific Railway v. Duluth, 208 U. S. 583.1
summary:
ERROR TO THE SUPREME COURT OF ¿THE STATE OF MINNESOTA.

This case involved a question almost the same as that in Northern Pacific Railway v. Duluth in which it was held that a railway was not deprived of its property without due process of law by being obliged to rebuild a viaduct over streets of a city.
attorneys: Mr. Rome G. Brown, with whom Mr. Charles S. Albert and Mr. William R. Begg were on the brief, for plaintiffs in error., Mr. Frank Healy, with whom Mr. Albert E. Clarke was on the brief, for defendant in error.

opinions.text:
Per Curiam:

Judgment affirmed on authority of Northern Pacific Railway Company v. State of Minnesota ex rel. Duluth, 208 U. S. 583.
